links.function: Generates ascending noradrenergic arousal pulses (locus coeruleus) that widen pupils even in pitch darkness.
links.narration_bridge: Deep inside the brainstem, a tiny autopilot hub sends micro wake-like pulses up every minute, pulling your hidden pupils wide even behind closed eyelids.

links.function: Generates 12-16 Hz sleep spindles that block external sounds from disturbing cortex when brainstem tone drops.
links.narration_bridge: When pupils shrink right before sleep spindles, the thalamus relay station slams shut against bedroom sounds like 45-decibel noise bursts.

links.function: Registers 30-45 Hz arousal slope shifts and slow-wave synchronization tracked by Fpz scalp electrodes.
links.narration_bridge: Front sensors sitting right over the spot behind the forehead moved in lockstep with pupil width as infraslow waves washed over the cortex.

links.function: Responds differently to gentle 45 dB pink-noise pulses depending on whether baseline brainstem pupil tone is calm or dilated.
links.narration_bridge: Only when baseline pupils sat quiet could soft tones push through the hearing center to strengthen restorative sleep rhythms.
